name: Kirloskar Ferrous Industries Ltd
title: Kirloskar Ferrous Industries Ltd - 500245 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Casting volumes up 19% and pig iron output up 5% with pricing improving, but tube sales down 14% and power-cost regulation hurting; supply additions are heavy and capex guided to Rs 600-700 crore this year.

summary.headline: Kirloskar Ferrous Q1 FY27: castings sales up 18% to 41,345 t, tube sales down 14% to 41,512 t, and power and fuel costs rose about INR58 crore YoY.
summary.overview: Pig iron and castings output rose in Q1 FY27, while tube output and sales fell on weaker high-value oil and gas and export orders. Power and fuel costs rose sharply, with about INR58 crore of the INR100 crore YoY jump in other expenses coming from power and fuel, half of it from rate increases. A change in green-power rules (8 hours instead of 17) and the end of power trading (about INR10 crore a year) cut the expected solar and wind savings to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore. Management guided to recovery in pricing and volumes from Q2, and said Q1 EBITDA margin was 12-13%.

financial_highlights.change: -3% YoY vs 132,392 t; management attributed to higher internal consumption
Company level; steel and tube margins cited at 14-17%

financial_highlights.metric: Power and fuel cost increase in other expenses
financial_highlights.value: INR58 crore of ~INR100 crore YoY jump
financial_highlights.change: About INR50 crore sequential jump in other expenses; about INR30 crore from rate increases

segments.name: Castings
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,345 t, up 18% YoY; pricing passed through to customers, with further price increases still being concluded. Rajpura foundry is fully sold out at about 2,200 t per month.

segments.name: Tubes
segments.commentary: Sales of 41,512 t, down 14% YoY, with a weaker product mix as more line pipe was sold in place of high-realising export and oil and gas tubes. Management is in a wait-and-watch stance due to Chinese dumping and subdued demand.

segments.name: Pig iron
segments.commentary: Realisation improved YoY and QoQ (about INR42,400/t vs INR39,000/t base, as cited on the call); about 30,000 t exported at slightly better than domestic prices. Pig iron EBITDA is expected to support the company margin.

segments.name: Steel (alloy)
segments.commentary: Management expects external sales of 100,000-110,000 t this year vs about 84,000 t, but cost pass-through is still under discussion.

guidance_outlook: Castings volumes expected to rise to about 162,000 t gross sales and then about 188,000 t, implying roughly 17-20% growth.
Overall volume growth of at least 15% across products in the remaining three quarters, with tube volumes up at least 10% YoY and steel external sales up more than 20%.
Pig iron output close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less.
Price-increase and cost pass-through benefits expected from Q2 and Q3 onward.

Medium term: about INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration with 300,000 t castings, 300,000 t casting sales and 400,000 t tube sales. Management said castings reach 270,000 t realisable capacity in this year plus two more years, with tubes at 350,000 t in 3-4 years.
Capex of INR600-700 crore this year, rising in the following years; about INR3,000-3,500 crore over the next four years.
capex_capacity: 35 MW solar plant in commissioning stage; 12 windmills of 2.1 MW each; both expected to be commissioned between June and September 2026.
Solapur two-part (no-bake) foundry, 15,000 t per annum, with commissioning expected by October 2026. Management said it has capacity of about 1,250 t per month.
Rajpura expansion: first phase to 40,000-50,000 t per annum within about 8 months; second phase to 70,000 t per annum. Total realisable castings capacity across six foundries is 270,000 t per annum.
Koppal oxygen plant and enhanced pulverised coal injection in blast furnaces 1 and 2, expected to complete by February-March 2027. Hiriyur pig iron upgrade to 360,000 t, taking about nine months.
Jejuri rolling capacity to rise from 15,000 t to 25,000 t per month (about 3 lakh t per annum), with about 240,000 t saleable; about 18-month timeline.

Premium couplings plant in Baramati, order expected within weeks. Koppal steel plant (about 2 years) and Baramati expander mill (2 years to build) are at early stages. Iron ore mines and pelletisation at Koppal are in progress.
One blast furnace to move to steelmaking, with government clearances in place; decision expected within 2-3 months, commissioning in about 2 years.
demand_pricing: Castings demand described as strong across tractors, automobiles, earthmoving equipment and stationary engines; management expects realisation improvement.
Tube demand subdued by oil and gas slowdown and export disruption; Chinese dumping is pressuring pricing. Management expects the tube market to recover.
Coke dumping into India has reportedly eased, which supports domestic pig iron prices. Pig iron exports are running at about 30,000 t.
Fuel costs rose sharply: LPG cost in Solapur roughly doubled versus pre-war levels. Coking coal cost is expected to peak in June-August because of a three-month coal inventory.
Monthly pig iron sales plan of about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external); foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t of that.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal (Unique PMS): what drove the ~INR100 crore YoY and ~INR50 crore QoQ jump in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR58 crore of the increase is power and fuel, split roughly INR28-29 crore rate-driven and INR28 crore volume-driven, with Rajpura castings volumes and a full-month Jejuri run versus last year's shutdown. Power trading (about INR10 crore a year) has stopped and green power use is now limited to 8 hours instead of 17.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal: does the regulation change hit the solar and wind savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, savings fall to about INR80 crore a year from about INR100 crore, and payback stretches from 3 years to 3.6-3.7 years. Battery storage at MW scale is being examined, with some power expected through batteries shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Nirmal: what is the INR350 crore contingent liability for forest development fee?
qa_highlights.answer: Karnataka levied forest development fees in 2016; the company won in the High Court, the state appealed to the Supreme Court, and the matter is sub judice after hearings with orders reserved. The company provides at 8% and discloses it as a contingent liability.

qa_highlights.question: Vipul Mody (individual investor): will the company move into subassemblies, machined components and high-end castings, and what is the status of 3D printing?
qa_highlights.answer: Machine shops at Koppal, Solapur and Rajpura already supply fully machined components, including a 6-cylinder head to an OEM. Maximum casting size after expansion is about 3 tons, the 2-part foundry is about 1,250 t per month, and the company is not yet in mining or wear-resistant parts. Prototyping is near serial production, with 50 cylinder blocks bought via the proto route.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co): what is Q1 EBITDA margin and how will it trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put Q1 company EBITDA at 12-13%, with steel and tube margins at 14-17% and pig iron weighing on the blend. Castings target about 15% plus or minus 1%, with pricing upside, and tubes are in a wait-and-watch phase due to Chinese dumping. Management expects company margin to improve on pig iron support and pass-through from Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: what are current pig iron realisations and how much did raw-material costs absorb?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisation moved from a base of about INR39,000/t to about INR42,400/t QoQ. Management said dollar rates and coal costs are pressuring costs, but realisation still improved slightly net of cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Dhruvesh Kanakia (Antique): what volumes are expected for the remaining nine months?
qa_highlights.answer: Pig iron close to 700,000 t this year, possibly slightly less. Castings gross sales to rise from about 162,000 t to about 188,000 t (17-20% growth). Steel external sales of 100,000-110,000 t vs about 84,000 t, and tube volumes up at least 10%, with overall volume growth of at least 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Manish Goyal (Thinkwise): timeline for INR14,000 crore revenue aspiration, seventh foundry, and ONGC/OIL tube order execution?
qa_highlights.answer: Castings realisable capacity of 270,000 t is targeted in this year plus two years, with 300,000 t in 3-4 years; tubes to 350,000 t in 3-4 years after the expander mill (2 years to build); steel external sales of 240,000 t in about 2 years. Blast furnace 1 conversion to steelmaking is expected to be decided within 2-3 months, with commissioning in about 2 years. The 23,000 t tube order should complete in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Sanghvi (Monarch): will coking coal costs rise further next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company holds about 3 months of coal stock, so the high-cost coal flows through June-August, which will be higher than April-June. Peaks may be partly mitigated as coal prices ease and blending improves.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Sanghvi: is pig iron realisation a blend of foundry and steel grade, and what is capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly pig iron sales plan is about 58,000 t including internal sales (about 48,000 t external), a mix of grades with foundry grade about 20,000-25,000 t. Capex is INR600-700 crore this year, rising in later years, with about INR3,000-3,500 crore over four years. Green power capex is set to slow, with battery storage starting at 50-70 MW.

qa_highlights.question: Anurag Patil (Quest): what is the net impact on annual power cost after solar, wind and power trading changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the 70 MW solar to yield INR70-80 crore a year, the 35 MW solar about INR30 crore, and the windmills (equivalent to 55 MW) to add more, with the combined solar and wind benefit at about INR70-80 crore. Seasonal wind benefit is about 70% in June-September. Koppal is self-sufficient on waste-heat power, but Maharashtra fuel costs need a strategy and power trading is not likely to return without battery storage.

risks_watch: Power and fuel cost inflation: about INR58 crore of YoY increase, LPG in Solapur roughly doubled, and coking coal peaking June-August; watch whether castings and alloy steel price pass-through actually lands in Q2-Q3.

Tube volume recovery: tube sales down 14% YoY with a weaker mix; Chinese dumping and subdued oil and gas and export demand; the INR100 crore-ish order book from ONGC/OIL is expected to finish within two quarters.

Green power economics: regulatory limit cut from 17 to 8 hours, power trading (about INR10 crore a year) stopped, and solar and wind savings cut to about INR80 crore from about INR100 crore; payback moved to 3.6-3.7 years.

Execution of capex: INR600-700 crore this year against INR3,000-3,500 crore over four years; Solapur 2-part foundry by October 2026, solar and wind commissioning June-September 2026, Koppal oxygen and PCI by February-March 2027.
Pig iron pricing and exports: realisation up to about INR42,400/t from INR39,000/t; about 30,000 t exported; a dollar and coal cost squeeze could offset gains.
Contingent liability of about INR350 crore on Karnataka forest development fee, sub judice at the Supreme Court with no timeline.
key_quotes: There's no understanding in the market for price escalation. So we have to really get the increase from the market for the tubes.
I think we are on this direction though still the aggregates could be a little far away.
So I would say that I'm optimistic and we should look for improved performance in the coming quarters.
We can't push too much of line pipes into market.
There is a negative impact, but we continue to progress because still there is benefit.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and forward-looking on pig iron pricing, castings demand and capacity expansion, but cautious on tubes, calling the market volatile and in a wait-and-watch stance. It was evasive on the exact tube volume and margin trajectory, and on the quantum of pricing pass-through for alloy steel.
